title: Capturing National Security Benefits from Offshore Wind
gist: A CSIS report (summary only available) assesses whether offshore wind infrastructure can act as a force multiplier for US maritime domain awareness amid growing drone and autonomous-vehicle threats, drawing on European sensor-integration lessons.

insights.claim: The report assesses whether offshore wind infrastructure can serve as a force multiplier for U.S. maritime domain awareness as autonomous vehicles and drones expand adversaries' reach and make critical maritime infrastructure more vulnerable.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: Security rationale could support offshore wind policy and sensor-supply demand.
insights.quote: force multiplier for U.S. maritime domain awareness

insights.claim: The report draws on European efforts to integrate sensors, share radar data and monitor subsea infrastructure.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: European precedents may guide US practice.

insights.claim: Dual-use deployment faces cost allocation, ownership and governance questions for sensors and data, and the risk that enhanced infrastructure itself becomes a target.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: Cost sharing and ownership are the key bottlenecks for developers.

insights.claim: The report offers initial recommendations for offshore wind developers, state governments and federal agencies, and is funded by The Pew Charitable Trusts.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: Funding source is relevant for assessing advocacy context.
